findings.title: No license file or license terms in the repository
findings.evidence:
project(GyroGuide)

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
set(EXTENSION_HOMEPAGE "https://www.slicer.org/slicerWiki/index.php/Documentation/Nightly/Extensions/GyroGuide")
findings.explanation: The repository file listing (root and GyroGuide/) has no LICENSE/COPYING file and no license header in the module. Without explicit terms, users and the Extensions Index have no permission to redistribute the extension. Under the index policy, missing distribution terms block approval.
findings.suggestion: Add a LICENSE file (any permissive or equivalent open license) at the repository root and a license header in GyroGuide.py.

items.title: No license terms anywhere in the repository

findings.title: No license terms anywhere in the repository
findings.evidence: An python extension of 3D Slicer which helps surgeons determine the puncture trajectory.
findings.explanation: A repository-wide search for license/copyright/GPL/BSD/MIT/Apache found no LICENSE/COPYING file and no license or copyright header in CMakeLists.txt, GyroGuide/CMakeLists.txt, GyroGuide.py or README.md. Without terms, the Extensions Index (and downstream packagers/mirrors) has no permission to redistribute the extension, and users have no statement of permitted use.
findings.suggestion: Add a LICENSE file (any OSI/permissive license the authors choose) and a matching header or README statement; confirm the authors own the code and the bundled icon.

items.title: Python 2 xrange used in the default Markups calculation path (NameError on Slicer 5)

findings.title: Python 2 `xrange` and legacy fiducial APIs make the module non-functional in current Slicer
findings.evidence:
self.p = numpy.zeros((n,3))

                for j in xrange(n):
findings.explanation: All three point-collection branches use `xrange` (lines 549, 577, 601), which does not exist in Python 3, so pressing Calculate on any fiducial node raises NameError and no result is produced in Slicer 5. The module also uses the pre-`ScriptedLoadableModule` template and Slicer 3/4 node classes (`vtkMRMLFiducialListNode`, `vtkMRMLAnnotationHierarchyNode`) and deprecated accessors, so it cannot deliver what the catalog description advertises.
findings.suggestion: Port to the current module template (`ScriptedLoadableModule`/`ScriptedLoadableModuleWidget`), replace `xrange` with `range`, and use vtkMRMLMarkupsNode APIs (GetNumberOfControlPoints/GetNthControlPointPosition); test in the targeted Slicer version.

findings.title: Python 2 xrange used in the default Markups calculation path (NameError on Slicer 5)
findings.explanation: Slicer 5 runs Python 3, where xrange is undefined. When the Markers/Target/Entry nodes are vtkMRMLMarkupsFiducialNode (the normal case, see the nodeTypes filter), the code reaches the loop using xrange and raises NameError. The Calculate button therefore fails before any result is shown.
findings.suggestion: Replace xrange with range (also at lines 549 and 601) and test the Calculate path in Slicer 5.

items.title: Angles computed in degrees are fed to numpy trig functions as radians

findings.title: Angles computed in degrees are fed to numpy trig functions as radians
findings.evidence:
theta = self.result.angleRed

        omega = self.result.angleGreen

        phi = self.result.angleBlue
findings.explanation: angleRed/Green/Blue are stored in degrees (arcsin * 180/pi). The transmission code then passes them to numpy.sin/numpy.cos, which expect radians. The rotation matrix sent to the OpenIGTLink device is therefore wrong, which could misdirect a navigation device during a procedure.
findings.suggestion: Convert the angles to radians (numpy.radians) before building the matrix, and add a unit test comparing the transform to the displayed angles.

items.title: Calculate deletes unrelated scene model nodes by name prefix

findings.title: Calculate deletes unrelated scene model nodes by name prefix
findings.evidence:
if modelName[i][0:5] == 'Plane' or modelName[i][0:8] == 'Puncture' or modelName[i][0:7] == 'Project' or modelName[i][0:4] == 'Line':



                scene.RemoveNode(model[i])
findings.explanation: Every model node in the scene whose name starts with 'Plane', 'Puncture', 'Project' or 'Line' is removed when the user presses Calculate - not just nodes created by this module (all its lines are even just named 'Line'). A user's own imported/model-maker output (e.g. 'Plane-anatomy', 'Line-of-approach') is silently destroyed in the scene, and the loss is unrecoverable if the scene was not saved; the same pattern removes any transform named 'Result-Data' (line 451-453). Because this happens without confirmation and in a planning workflow, it is a concrete path to losing patient-derived data.
findings.suggestion: Track the node IDs the module creates and delete only those (or store them under a dedicated subject hierarchy folder), instead of matching name prefixes; prompt before removing nodes the module did not create.

items.title: Clinical guidance output with no disclaimer; blocking GUI sleeps

findings.title: Send handler blocks the GUI thread with fixed sleeps
findings.evidence:
time.sleep(1)

        matrix.DeepCopy((e1,e2,e3,e4,e5,e6,e7,e8,e9,e10,e11,e12,0,0,0,1))

        time.sleep(1)

        connectorNode.Stop()
findings.explanation: The OpenIGTLink send runs in the button-click slot and freezes Slicer's event loop for two seconds per press, with no progress feedback; the fixed delays are also a fragile substitute for waiting for an actual message handshake.
findings.suggestion: Push the transform through the connector node without sleep, or run the send asynchronously (e.g. qt.QTimer / cli node) with progress and a status message.

findings.title: Clinical guidance output with no disclaimer; blocking GUI sleeps
findings.evidence:
time.sleep(1)

        matrix.DeepCopy((e1,e2,e3,e4,e5,e6,e7,e8,e9,e10,e11,e12,0,0,0,1))

        time.sleep(1)
findings.explanation: The module reports puncture depth and angles and transmits them to a navigation device, but has no statement that it is research-only or not validated. The Send handler blocks the GUI thread with time.sleep(1) twice, so Slicer can freeze while sending, and a wrong transform could be used for navigation.
findings.suggestion: Add a clinical-use disclaimer in helpText and the README, remove the sleeps (or use a Qt timer), and check the transform before sending.

items.title: Surgical trajectory tool ships without documentation, validation or clinical disclaimer

findings.title: Surgical trajectory tool ships without documentation, validation or clinical disclaimer
findings.evidence:
GyroGuide
=========

An python extension of 3D Slicer which helps surgeons determine the puncture trajectory.
findings.explanation: The module computes puncture angle/depth for neurosurgical puncture and drives an external navigation probe, yet the repository provides only a one-sentence README, no tutorial or sample data, no accuracy/validation evidence, and no statement that it is not approved for clinical use. At tier 3 (community supported), users have no way to judge correctness or suitability for patient care.
findings.suggestion: Add usage documentation with sample data, describe how the angles are defined and validated, and include an explicit research/not-for-clinical-use disclaimer until validation is published.

items.title: CMake registers a unittest on a script that contains no tests; real test target is commented out

findings.title: CMake registers a unittest on a script that contains no tests; real test target is commented out
findings.evidence:
if(BUILD_TESTING)

    # Register the unittest subclass in the main script as a ctest.

    # Note that the test will also be available at runtime.

    slicer_add_python_unittest(SCRIPT ${MODULE_NAME}.py)
findings.explanation: GyroGuide.py defines no unittest.TestCase subclass, so the registered ctest has nothing to run, and GyroGuide/Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt only contains a commented-out line, leaving the extension without any automated test at tier 3.
findings.suggestion: Add a real ScriptedLoadableModuleTest (or the standard ModuleTest.py) and register it, so the extension has a passing smoke test.

items.title: Calculator returns early but callers assume results exist; 5-marker assumption unchecked

findings.title: Calculator returns early but callers assume results exist; 5-marker assumption unchecked
findings.evidence:
vector1 = self.position[0][0] - self.position[0][1] #a vector in the plane red

        vector2 = self.position[0][0] - self.position[0][2] #a vector in the plane red
findings.explanation: If any selected node has zero points the constructor `return`s (lines 545, 569, 595) leaving `self.position` short, so the following indexing raises IndexError/AttributeError; likewise markers nodes with fewer than five points make `self.position[0][3] - self.position[0][4]` (line 617) fail. The UI enables Calculate for any node with a valid type, so these exceptions reach the user as raw tracebacks.
findings.suggestion: Validate point counts (>=5 markers, >=1 target, >=1 entry, distinct points, non-zero-length vectors) and report a clear message via slicer.util.errorDisplay instead of continuing.

findings.title: Too few markers raises an IndexError with no user message
findings.evidence:
vector1 = self.position[0][0] - self.position[0][1] #a vector in the plane red

        vector2 = self.position[0][0] - self.position[0][2] #a vector in the plane red
findings.explanation: The calculation indexes fiducials 0 through 4 of the marker list, and target/entry index 0. A list with fewer than five markers raises IndexError inside the Calculate handler, and no message explains the requirement.
findings.suggestion: Validate the number of markers (5) and target/entry points (1 each) and show a message box.

items.title: Connector-node lookup creates duplicate connector nodes

findings.title: Connector-node lookup creates duplicate connector nodes
findings.explanation: The else branch is inside the loop, so for every connector node not named 'Send-Data' a new node is created and added; with N existing connectors the scene accumulates extra 'Send-Data' nodes and only the last one is used. Also, `vtkMRMLIGTLConnectorNode` is used without checking that the OpenIGTLink extension is installed.
findings.suggestion: Look the node up once outside the loop (e.g. via GetFirstNodeByName) and create it only if absent; guard for a missing vtkMRMLIGTLConnectorNode class.

findings.title: Connector and transform nodes accumulate on each Send
findings.explanation: The connector loop creates a new vtkMRMLIGTLConnectorNode for every existing connector that is not named 'Send-Data', so repeated Send clicks add nodes to the scene. Result transform nodes are also re-created each time.
findings.suggestion: Look up or create a single connector node once, and reuse or update the existing transform node.

items.title: Legacy module structure and unpinned source revision

findings.title: Legacy module structure and unpinned source revision
findings.evidence: from __main__ import vtk, qt, ctk, slicer
findings.explanation: The module uses plain classes with 'from __main__ import' rather than ScriptedLoadableModule, which is fragile on current Slicer. The catalog pins scm_revision to the branch 'master', so the built code can change without a catalog update.
findings.suggestion: Port to ScriptedLoadableModule and pin scm_revision to a specific commit hash.

items.title: No active tests and minimal documentation

findings.title: No active tests and minimal documentation
findings.evidence: #slicer_add_python_unittest(SCRIPT ${MODULE_NAME}ModuleTest.py)
findings.explanation: WITH_GENERIC_TESTS is set, but the module has no test class and the Testing registration is commented out. The README is one sentence, and no sample data or tutorial is included, so maintainers and users cannot verify the geometry.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test with synthetic fiducials and expected angles and depth, and expand the README with usage and a disclaimer.

items.title: OpenIGTLink connection failure is silently ignored

findings.title: OpenIGTLink connection failure is silently ignored
findings.evidence:
hostname = self.hostnameLineEdit.text

        port = int(self.portLineEdit.text)

        connectorNode.SetTypeClient(hostname, port)

        checker = connectorNode.Start()
findings.explanation: The result of Start() is never checked and no error is shown, so if the device is unreachable the transform is registered and then the connector is stopped without the user knowing nothing was delivered; a non-numeric port raises an uncaught ValueError from `int(...)` in the GUI click handler.
findings.suggestion: Validate the port, check the Start() return value and surface connection failures with slicer.util.errorDisplay / warning; disable Send until a connection succeeds.

items.title: Bundled icon is not installed and not used by the code

findings.title: Bundled icon is not installed and not used by the code
findings.evidence:
set(MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES

  )
findings.explanation: GyroGuide/Resources/Icons/GyroGuide.png is committed but MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES is empty and no code references the icon, so it is dead weight (a duplicate of the root GyroGuide.png); the catalog uses a wiki URL for the icon instead.
findings.suggestion: Either remove the unused Resources icon or install it via MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES and use it as the module icon.
